Lessons.Title: Introducing the Number $i$
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Comprehend that the symbol “$i$” means the positive square root of -1 and that an imaginary number is a real number times $i$. Represent solutions to equations using $i$ and the complex plane.
A complex value a+bi corresponds to point (a,b); the horizontal component is real, vertical imaginary and i²=-1.

Source activity 11.1: Math Talk: Squared: Find the value of each expression mentally. \(\left(2\sqrt{3}\right)^2\) \(\left(\frac12 \sqrt{3}\right)^2\) \(\left(2\sqrt{\text- 1}\right)^2\) \(\left(\frac12 \sqrt{\text- 1}\right)^2\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 11.2: It is $i$: Find the solutions to these equations, then plot the solutions to each equation on the imaginary or real number line. Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 11.3: The $i$’s Have It: Write these imaginary numbers using the number \(i\). \(\sqrt{\text- 36}\) \(\sqrt{\text- 10}\) \(\text- \sqrt{\text- 100}\) \(\text- \sqrt{\text- 17}\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 11.4: Complex Numbers: Label at least 8 different imaginary numbers on the imaginary number line. When we add a real number and an imaginary number, we get a complex number. The diagram shows where \(2 + i\) is in the complex number plane. What complex number is represented by point \(A\)? Plot these complex numbers in the complex number plane and label them. Diego says that all real numbers and all… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.
Practice Problem 1: Which point represents the complex number \(\text-3 + 2i\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 2: Match each expression to an equivalent expression. \(2i \boldcdot 8i\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Diego squared a number and got 4. Andre squared a different number and got 4. What were the numbers that Diego and Andre squared? Jada squared a number and got -4. Elena squared a different number and got -4. What were the numbers that Jada and Elena squared? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 4: Find all solutions to each equation. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: Find the exact solution(s) to each of these equations, or explain why there is no solution. \(\sqrt[3]{a+2}=4\) \(\sqrt[3]{b} +5 = 4\) \(\sqrt[3]{c-1}-14=\text-4\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 6: Explain how you know that \(\sqrt{\text-1}\) is not a negative number. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Edulytics independent cool-down: Solve x²=-16 over complex numbers. Expected reasoning or answer: x=±4i.
